paragraphs.text: Hospitals are rethinking the design of their wards. Architect Laura Stein argues that single rooms should replace large shared wards, because patients sleep better and infections spread less easily when each person has their own space.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Nurse manager Paul Okoro is not convinced. He points out that nurses can see many patients at once on an open ward, and that in single rooms, patients who suddenly become unwell may not be noticed as quickly.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A study by the National Health Research Institute compared both designs in six hospitals. It found fewer infections in single rooms but no difference in how long patients stayed, and it concluded that the higher building costs were justified only for certain patients.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Patient groups add another view. The Patients’ Voice charity reports that older patients often feel lonely in single rooms and would prefer small shared bays of four beds, a design that Stein says she is willing to include.
paragraphs.label: D

items.quote: patients who suddenly become unwell may not be noticed as quickly
items.prompt: is worried that staff may miss a change in a patient’s condition

explanation.en: Nurse manager Okoro worries that in single rooms “patients who suddenly become unwell may not be noticed as quickly”. That is the risk of missing a change → B.
explanation.kk: Мейірбикелер басшысы Окоро жеке палатада «patients who suddenly become unwell may not be noticed as quickly» деп алаңдайды. Бұл — науқастың нашарлағанын байқамай қалу қаупі → B.
explanation.ru: Медсестра-руководитель Окоро опасается, что в отдельных палатах «patients who suddenly become unwell may not be noticed as quickly». Это и есть риск упустить ухудшение → B.

items.quote: no difference in how long patients stayed
items.prompt: found that one design did not shorten hospital stays
keywords: no difference in how long patients stayed

explanation.en: The institute’s study found “no difference in how long patients stayed” → C. Stein talks about sleep and infection, not length of stay.
explanation.kk: Институт зерттеуі «no difference in how long patients stayed» екенін көрсеткен → C. Стайн ұйқы мен инфекция туралы айтады, мерзім туралы емес.
explanation.ru: Исследование института показало «no difference in how long patients stayed» → C. Стайн говорит о сне и инфекциях, но не о сроках.

items.quote: older patients often feel lonely in single rooms
items.prompt: reports that some patients feel alone

explanation.en: The patients’ charity reports that “older patients often feel lonely in single rooms” → D.
explanation.kk: Науқастар қайырымдылық ұйымы: «older patients often feel lonely in single rooms» → D.
explanation.ru: Благотворительная организация пациентов: «older patients often feel lonely in single rooms» → D.

items.quote: patients sleep better and infections spread less easily when each person has their own space
items.prompt: says patients rest better in private rooms

explanation.en: Stein: in single rooms “patients sleep better” → A. “Rest better” paraphrases “sleep better”.
explanation.kk: Стайн: жеке палатада «patients sleep better» → A. «Rest better» — «sleep better» дегеннің басқаша айтылымы.
explanation.ru: Стайн: в отдельных палатах «patients sleep better» → A. «Rest better» пересказывает «sleep better».

items.quote: a design that Stein says she is willing to include
items.prompt: is prepared to accept a compromise design

explanation.en: Small four-bed bays are a compromise “Stein says she is willing to include” → A. The charity (D) proposes it, but Stein is the one accepting it.
explanation.kk: Төрт төсектік шағын палата — ымыра, оны «Stein says she is willing to include» → A. Оны қайырымдылық ұйымы (D) ұсынады, ал келісім білдіретін — Стайн.
explanation.ru: Маленькие палаты на четыре кровати — компромисс, который «Stein says she is willing to include» → A. Предлагает его благотворительная организация (D), а согласие выражает Стайн.
